inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,849 normalized logical lines of Berry and Keating's 1999 review. The usable source develops four linked strands: the explicit prime/periodic-orbit trace-formula analogy and its tensions; long-orbit universality plus short-orbit and arithmetic corrections to zero statistics; Riemann-Siegel resurgence and quantum spectral-determinant resummation; and a property-by-property, explicitly incomplete XP candidate dynamics. Formula extraction is imperfect but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose and adjacent displayed equations. The enormous printed C20 coefficient, page furniture, and bibliography are accounted for without being promoted.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata and an abstract preview of the spectral analogy, universality, Riemann-Siegel resurgence, and XP speculation.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the bidirectional prime-chaos-spectrum analogy, derives the prime-density frequency viewpoint, and motivates a self-adjoint spectral interpretation of real zero heights.

sections_inspected.label: 2. The Analogy
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the formal dictionary between the Riemann counting formula and chaotic trace formula, including scaling, stability, symmetry, phase, smooth density, and Heisenberg-time consequences.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Long Orbits and Universality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects orbit proliferation and the Hannay-Ozorio sum rule to GUE-scale universality while locating system-specific breakdown at the shortest-orbit scale.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Periodic-Orbit Theory for Spectral Statistics
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops form-factor and correlation calculations, separates diagonal and off-diagonal mechanisms, derives arithmetic and dynamical nonuniversal corrections, and extends the picture to higher correlations.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Riemann-Siegel Formulae
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains stationary truncation, resurgence, high-order divergence and optimal truncation, then transfers the resummation mechanism to pseudo-orbit spectral determinants and complex orbits.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Spectral Speculations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Collects inferred constraints on a Riemann dynamics and tests the XP Hamiltonian, its quantization, Fourier duality, dilation symmetries, possible compactifications, and unresolved failures.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support only; no independent semantic unit is selected from citation entries.

accepted_units.title: A bidirectional spectral-dynamical-prime analogy
accepted_units.why_material: Frames the zeros as putative wave eigenvalues of an unknown chaotic dynamics and stresses that even without identifying the system, inferred properties transmit useful information between spectral physics and prime-number theory.
accepted_units.context_note: The claim is explicitly tentative; the statement that identifying the system would prove RH is the authors' route claim, not an accomplished construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is self-contained; no formula reconstruction is required.

accepted_units.title: Prime density as oscillations indexed by complex zero heights
accepted_units.why_material: Moves from the prime staircase through prime powers and the explicit formula to oscillatory density contributions indexed by zeta zeros, exposing how zero location controls frequency and damping.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the local definitions of the zeta function, critical strip, critical line, and tn needed to interpret the oscillatory representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (1.1)-(1.6) are extraction-sensitive, but their roles and variables are recoverable from adjacent prose; verify against the PDF for symbol-exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic reparameterization turns RH into discreteness of a prime spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: The substitution u=log x removes slowing oscillations; under RH the prime-derived signal has discrete Fourier support, motivating the Hilbert-Polya question of which self-adjoint system has these frequencies.
accepted_units.context_note: The acoustic metaphor is retained only as a bridge to the operator question, not as computational evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (1.7) carries OCR risk, but the discrete-versus-nondiscrete spectrum consequence is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Smooth and fluctuating parts of the zero counting function
accepted_units.why_material: Separates N(t) into a secular mean governed by the functional equation and a zero-mean fluctuation from the argument of zeta, while defining the asymptotically local averaging scale used throughout.
accepted_units.context_note: The initial assumption that tn are real is part of the analogy's working condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed gamma, density, and log-zeta formulae should be checked in the source PDF before exact symbolic use; the decomposition is prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: A divergent prime-power orbit-like expansion can resolve zeros when truncated
accepted_units.why_material: Formally inserts the Euler product in the critical strip to express Nfl as prime-power oscillations, identifies periods 2π/log p, and links resolution of individual zeros to a t-dependent prime cutoff despite divergence of the full series.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly calls the substitution nonconvergent and the expression formally exact; this caveat is essential.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (2.6)-(2.7) are needed for exact amplitudes and periods and retain formula-extraction risk.

accepted_units.title: Chaotic periodic orbits determine semiclassical spectral fluctuations
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces Hamiltonian wave quantization, isolated unstable periodic orbits, and the trace formula in which actions, periods, stability matrices, repetitions, and Maslov phases generate counting fluctuations.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the quantum side of the later Riemann dictionary and includes the ergodic energy-surface versus periodic-orbit distinction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The trace formula and determinant asymptotics are formula-dependent and should be scan-verified for exact notation; explanatory prose is intact.

accepted_units.title: Prime powers map to repetitions of uniformly unstable, non-time-reversal-symmetric orbits
accepted_units.why_material: Matches actions, periods, stabilities, and asymptotic parameters term by term, inferring prime-labelled primitive orbits of period log p, unit instability exponent, scaling dynamics, and absence of time-reversal symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: These are constraints inferred from formal coefficient matching, not evidence that an underlying Hamiltonian has been constructed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The correspondence table (2.14) is visually degraded; the surrounding prose fixes the intended mapping.

accepted_units.title: Two discordances constrain any literal trace-formula realization
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts the analogy in density form and isolates two nontrivial mismatches: exponential stability is approximate for generic long orbits but exact arithmetically, and the required negative sign conflicts with repetition behavior of Maslov phases.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit preserves the source's warning against treating formal similarity as a completed dynamical model.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact amplitudes in (2.16)-(2.18) are formula-dependent, though both discordances are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Heisenberg time sets the orbit length needed to resolve individual levels
accepted_units.why_material: Combines Weyl cell counting, orbit-induced energy wavelengths, and mean spacing to show that level resolution requires orbits through the Heisenberg time, corresponding on the Riemann side to primes up to t/2π.
accepted_units.context_note: This scale relation motivates why long-orbit statistics, rather than a few short orbits, control microscopic spectral structure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula symbols are moderately extraction-sensitive; the asymptotic comparison is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Orbit proliferation cancels amplitude decay to produce a universal sum rule
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how exponential proliferation and squared-amplitude decay balance in the Hannay-Ozorio rule, relates it to ergodicity, Perron-Frobenius invariance and a dynamical-zeta pole, and transfers the resulting microscopic universality expectation to the zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: System-specific approach rates remain encoded away from the invariant pole.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (3.1)-(3.3) need formula verification for exact normalization; the cancellation and operator interpretation are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Within-spectrum GUE universality is nonuniform and breaks at the shortest-orbit scale
accepted_units.why_material: Clarifies how statistics arise from local spectral averaging without an ensemble, identifies GUE for chaotic systems lacking time reversal, and predicts loss of universality at separations controlled by the shortest orbit, log 2 for the zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Agreement with observed breakdown is reported as support for the analogy, not as proof of RH or of a unique operator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The scale estimate is formula-assisted but fully described in prose.

accepted_units.title: Pair correlation, form factor, and number variance are interchangeable bilinear views
accepted_units.why_material: Defines local unfolding and three linked spectral statistics, with Fourier duality between pair correlation and form factor and an integral relation to number variance, establishing the observables used to separate universal and nonuniversal structure.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is setup rather than a conclusion, but it is necessary to reuse the later mechanisms without reconstructing definitions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed formula lines have reading-order damage; exact definitions must be checked against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: The diagonal approximation yields GUE only before the Heisenberg time
accepted_units.why_material: Substitution of the trace formula creates a double orbit sum; diagonal terms plus the universal sum rule give K=|τ| and match GUE for |τ|<1, while discreteness forces coherent off-diagonal cancellation for longer times.
accepted_units.context_note: The source distinguishes Montgomery's proved diagonal regime from the conjectured full GUE form.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The derivation depends on equations (4.5)-(4.12), whose layout should be scan-verified, but the diagonal/off-diagonal logic is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair correlations supply the missing off-diagonal coherence
accepted_units.why_material: Shows why uncorrelated prime-orbit phases would kill off-diagonal terms and how the arithmetic deviation of the prime-pair factor from randomness yields the cancellation required by the GUE form factor.
accepted_units.context_note: The result is conditional on the cited Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic and is presented as a derivation under that conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and products in (4.13)-(4.16) are formula-dependent and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Short orbits restore system-specific statistics beyond the universal window
accepted_units.why_material: Splices direct short-orbit contributions into the universal form factor, producing a nonuniform correction that accurately tracks the transition from random-matrix behavior to long-range Riemann-zero statistics.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed formula is immediately flagged as incomplete near τ=1 because its off-diagonal treatment is only limiting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (4.18) and figure annotations are extraction-sensitive; the construction and caveat are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: High-zero correlations contain low zeros as nonuniversal resonances
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the diagonal correction using the zeta function near 1, separating primitive and repeated contributions and revealing low Riemann zeros as resonances in pair correlations and number variance high in the spectrum.
accepted_units.context_note: The prefactor makes the correction asymptotically small even though its structured resonances move to large unfolded separations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The closed formula (4.23) is symbol-sensitive; its five structural consequences are enumerated reliably in prose.

accepted_units.title: Perron-Frobenius resonances are the dynamical analogue of low-zero resurgence
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers the zeta correction to generic chaotic dynamics: the invariant dynamical-zeta pole cancels the local singularity, while other singularities, equivalently subdominant Perron-Frobenius eigenvalues, cause nonuniversal resonances.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a generic-system analogue, not a claim that the unknown Riemann dynamics has been identified.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact normalization of (4.25) is formula-dependent; the pole/resonance interpretation is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Unsmoothed prime-pair arithmetic produces the small off-diagonal oscillation correction
accepted_units.why_material: Explains that using the full Hardy-Littlewood factor rather than its average adds a convergent Euler-product correction that recovers tiny observed oscillations, while emphasizing why the same derivation cannot simply be copied to unknown generic orbit correlations.
accepted_units.context_note: Working backward from assumed GUE predicts only a universal limiting action correlation and gives no system-specific deviations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (4.27)-(4.28) and figure comparisons should be scan-verified; the methodological limitation is textual.

accepted_units.title: A truncated trace formula defines an approximate spectrum whose correlations can be computed
accepted_units.why_material: Uses orbits shorter than the Heisenberg time to reconstruct approximate eigenvalues and treats their contributions as effectively uncorrelated, yielding generic diagonal and off-diagonal corrections and a heuristic route back to Hardy-Littlewood-type orbit correlations.
accepted_units.context_note: The source calls the inverse derivation heuristic and leaves a classical derivation of the predicted correlations open.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The q-hypergeometric product formula is extraction-fragile; the two-observation method and inference direction are prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: GUE universality and nonuniversal zeta structure extend to n-point correlations
accepted_units.why_material: Extends the two-point picture to determinant-form n-point GUE limits, separating proved diagonal results, conjecture-dependent off-diagonal calculations, and zeta-near-one corrections for higher correlations.
accepted_units.context_note: The evidence status varies across diagonal theorems, generalized Hardy-Littlewood inputs, and calculated deviations; the unit preserves those distinctions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The determinant and kernel equations are formula-dependent but legible enough for semantic planning.

accepted_units.title: Stationary truncation and tail resurgence repair the formal critical-line series
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the real Hardy Z-function, diagnoses nonconvergence and hidden reality in the naive Dirichlet series, then truncates at the stationary term so the resummed tail becomes the conjugate of the early terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Successive partial main sums improve zero positions but can have complex zeros, so they are not spectra of approximating Hermitian operators.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The cutoff and main-sum equations are formula-dependent and should be verified for exact constants.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel correction terms smooth truncation discontinuities
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why abrupt stationary truncation breaks analyticity and constructs an inverse-a asymptotic series whose coefficient functions derive from derivatives of a base function and a Bernoulli-driven recurrence.
accepted_units.context_note: The few displayed low-order coefficients illustrate the construction; later coefficient bulk is not itself a separate semantic mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Derivative superscripts and coefficient layout are OCR-sensitive; exact symbolic reuse requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Factorial late terms determine an exponentially small optimal error
accepted_units.why_material: Compresses high-order coefficients into a decorated factorial asymptotic, identifies divergence after a least term, and uses Borel-supported optimal truncation to obtain an exp(-πt) error scale.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding giant C20 printout is routine evidence of complexity; this span captures its reusable large-order meaning.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (5.10)-(5.13) carry formula risk, but factorial growth, least-term truncation, and error scale are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Quantum spectral determinants turn primitive orbits into pseudo-orbit Dirichlet terms
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a real spectral determinant, expands the trace formula into composite pseudo-orbits analogous to integers built from primes, and derives a stationary cutoff at half the Heisenberg time.
accepted_units.context_note: The spectral determinant expansion is semiclassical and divergent before resummation, unlike an exact finite operator identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product, determinant, and pseudo-orbit equations are notation-sensitive; the prime/pseudo-orbit correspondence is clearly narrated.

accepted_units.title: Long pseudo-orbits resurge from short ones, but proliferation limits computation
accepted_units.why_material: Pairs groups around the half-Heisenberg cutoff so the long tail is approximately the conjugate of the short pseudo-orbit sum, producing a real finite Riemann-Siegel lookalike while exposing exponential term proliferation and remaining discontinuities.
accepted_units.context_note: The source distinguishes conceptual resummation value from practical high-energy efficiency and notes no correction series analogous to Cr was known.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (5.23) is formula-dependent; limitations are prose-explicit.

accepted_units.title: Error-function smoothing gives a transferable completion of abrupt resummation
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces the hard cutoff by a complementary-error-function window, improves the attainable zeta accuracy, and transfers the analytic-continuation construction to quantum spectral determinants with reported near-degenerate-level resolution.
accepted_units.context_note: Accuracy claims concern the cited representation and numerical test, not a solution of the unknown Riemann operator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Erfc arguments and derivative notation in (5.24)-(5.25) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The exponentially small Riemann-Siegel remainder suggests imaginary-period orbits
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets exp(-πt) as a semiclassical phase with imaginary action, inferring complex periodic orbits with periods that are multiples of iπ in addition to the real prime-log periods.
accepted_units.context_note: The source presents this as a quantum-mechanical clue, not a constructed orbit in a known phase space.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The action-to-period differentiation is compact and formula-dependent but readable.

accepted_units.title: Trace and statistical analogies impose a detailed Riemann-dynamics checklist
accepted_units.why_material: Collects required properties: Hamiltonian or symplectic origin, bounded chaos, broken time reversal, homogeneous instability, prime-log periodic orbits, anomalous phases, complex orbits, exact leading semiclassics, quasi-one-dimensional growth, and a functional-equation/hermiticity parallel.
accepted_units.context_note: The list is an inference ledger; several entries are explicitly peculiar or unexplained rather than mutually realized.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primarily prose; the quasi-one-dimensional evidence refers back to formula amplitudes.

accepted_units.title: Classical XP matches instability and mean counting only after an ad hoc cutoff
accepted_units.why_material: The flow of XP is uniformly hyperbolic and non-time-reversible, and Planck-cell area under a truncated energy hyperbola reproduces the smoothed zero count including its constant term, but the unbounded phase space prevents a discrete spectrum.
accepted_units.context_note: The source calls bounding or compactifying the motion a central unsolved problem; the cutoff is an interim expedient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations of motion and the phase-space area argument depend on the displayed XP representation; prose fixes the limitation.

accepted_units.title: Symmetric quantization of XP places its power-law eigenfunctions on the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: The formally Hermitian dilation generator has monomial eigenfunctions X^{-1/2+iE}, echoing n^{-s} and p^{-s}; symmetrization supplies the one-half real part, and canonical rotation links the model to the inverted oscillator.
accepted_units.context_note: Formal Hermiticity and generalized eigenfunctions do not provide self-adjoint boundary conditions or a discrete Riemann spectrum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Operator signs and exponents in (6.3)-(6.5) must be checked against the PDF for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Fourier duality recovers the theta phase but leaves compactification unresolved
accepted_units.why_material: With even continuation across X=0, the Fourier-transformed momentum eigenfunction is the time reverse of the position eigenfunction and carries the zeta functional-equation phase, while the required self-adjoint discrete boundary condition remains equivalent to closing phase space.
accepted_units.context_note: The parity continuation is chosen rather than derived and is motivated only by later complex-orbit considerations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gamma ratios and phase factors in (6.6) are formula-sensitive; the duality interpretation is textual.

accepted_units.title: Sign identification and dilation symmetry offer hints but not a boundary condition
accepted_units.why_material: Identifying X with -X halves the complex XP period to the desired iπ, while continuous dilation symmetry makes time evolution logarithmic; restricting to integer dilations can insert zeta into a superposition but neither forces its vanishing nor forms a group.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors explicitly describe the symmetry-superposition program as unrealized.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The generator identity (6.8) has extraction complexity; the group-theoretic failures are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Modular dilation characters suggest L-functions as self-adjoint extensions
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces non-group integer dilations by multiplicative residue-class groups and interprets their characters as discrete extension phases, potentially assigning different Dirichlet L-functions to different self-adjoint extensions of XP.
accepted_units.context_note: The Bloch-Floquet analogy is explicitly imperfect and no actual extension domain or spectral theorem is supplied.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The L-series equation is straightforward but character and extension claims remain speculative prose.

accepted_units.title: Canonical position-momentum exchange yields an almost-correct zero condition
accepted_units.why_material: Proposes closing XP motion by reinjecting asymptotic position flow through momentum, derives an XP-preserving exchange and a functional-equation identity, then exposes a decisive sign mismatch that prevents it from generating the zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors do not know how to turn the quantum exchange into an effective boundary condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (6.10)-(6.12) are formula- and sign-sensitive; PDF verification is mandatory for exact use.

accepted_units.title: XP satisfies many inferred constraints but misses boundedness, primes, and phase structure
accepted_units.why_material: Performs a concise property-by-property audit: XP has the right instability, symmetry breaking, scaling-related features and several analytic parallels, yet remains unbounded and offers no clear primitive-prime mechanism or explanation of the anomalous Maslov phases.
accepted_units.context_note: This negative ledger prevents the attractive XP correspondences from being mistaken for a completed spectral realization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Self-contained prose referring to the earlier constraint list.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From explicit formula to a constrained trace-formula dictionary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Matching the two counting fluctuations identifies primes with primitive periods and fixes scaling, stability, symmetry, and resolution scales, while the exact-amplitude and Maslov-sign discordances sharply constrain any literal spectral realization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is formal coefficient matching with divergent/asymptotic inputs; it neither constructs an operator nor proves that all zeros are real.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universality is generated by long-orbit balance and corrected by arithmetic short structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The orbit sum rule explains microscopic GUE behavior, off-diagonal prime correlations restore discreteness beyond the diagonal regime, and short-orbit or dynamical-zeta data encode structured nonuniversal deviations including low-zero resonances.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several off-diagonal steps depend on Hardy-Littlewood-type conjectures or assumed GUE behavior, and generic classical action correlations are not derived from first principles here.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Riemann-Siegel resurgence becomes a pseudo-orbit spectral-determinant principle
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Reality reorganizes a divergent long expansion around a stationary half-Heisenberg cutoff: long terms resurge as conjugates of short ones, while late-term divergence dictates optimal truncation and smoothing produces a transferable quantum completion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The quantum lookalike remains semiclassical, computationally burdened by exponential pseudo-orbit proliferation, and does not supply the unknown Riemann operator.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: XP is a constraint-matching prototype whose missing boundary mechanism is decisive
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: XP naturally realizes dilation, uniform instability, broken time reversal, critical-line power laws, functional-equation phase, and the mean count after regularization, but every attempted compactification leaves missing boundedness, prime-orbit generation, anomalous phases, or a sign-correct zero condition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The proposal is explicitly speculative and formally Hermitian only; no self-adjoint discrete realization with the Riemann zeros is obtained.

within_source_saturation: Whole-source saturation reached after representing every distinct mechanism, transfer, caveat, and failed route in the six mathematical sections. Further splitting would mainly isolate algebraic steps already attached to their governing argument, repeat figure-level evidence, promote extraction-fragile coefficient detail, or mine bibliography rather than add a new reusable semantic move.
stop_reason: The article's substantive text ends with its explicit XP property audit at line 1687, followed by a transition and references. All earlier prose and displayed-equation regions are assigned to accepted units or coverage dispositions; the only deliberately unselected mathematical bulk is the routine C20 coefficient printout, whose semantic role is captured by the recurrence and factorial late-term units.
